story.intro:
Aethelgard
The forge of the missing master Valerius

ending.heartfire:
The crystals burn away in the Heartfire.
For a moment, Nox's runes glow in time with the flames.
ending.done:
You did it!

You brought Nox to life and guided him all the way to the Heartfire.
Variables, loops, methods and conditions were your tools.

The Soulweavers' Legacy is complete.
Click to end your journey.

story.letter:
In case anyone is looking for me: I have gone to the Heartfire.

The second exit is stuck. Rubble is blocking the gate winch in the cellar, and hot steam is leaking from the old pipes. Do not go down there yourselves.

I built Nox for work like this. He carries loads and keeps the machines clear. His soul binding has gone out, though. Vessels and essences are in the workshop chests.

Restore his soul binding. He is to clear the gate winch so that the exit can be opened again.

Valerius
story.archive:
Work order · Machine cellar

Nox: clear the conveyor track, the pump access and the chain hoist. Cross the damaged cooling channel, then remove the rubble at the gate winch.

The brass markers are his work positions. The arrows show which way he must face. The control program has to end completely there. Only then does the separate clearing job begin. Merely touching a marker is not enough.

Control programs are kept in the archive, among them old test runs. The control book takes one rhythm rune at a time. If the run does not fit the job, Nox returns to his last work position. The rune is kept. While he is moving or returning, he accepts no new program.

The viewing stone transmits his view from the cellar. The map only reports where an obstacle lies.

Valerius
story.maintenance:
Maintenance, gate winch

The lower bracket is badly rusted. It gives way under load.

Valerius
story.workshop:
The gate winch is destroyed. We still have the workshop's side exit. Activate the rune stones, collect their crystals and supply both altars.

Valerius' long program already does all that. But the exit control holds only eight commands in the main program. Move repeated sequences into methods of your own. Their calls save space. Parameters and return values make the same method usable several times.

The workshop is a test bench. Every start resets Nox and all objects. Open the control book on the workbench and try out your changes.
story.workshop-journal:
Valerius' workshop journal

The complete program is in the control book. Two gates, the same task twice. The runes require different directions. The fields yield three and five crystals. The altars need exactly these amounts.

The exit control has room for eight commands. Methods of your own have their own memory. I must combine the repetitions and pass their differences as parameters. A collection hands back its actual count as a return value.

The test bench resets everything before each run. Errors stay visible until the next attempt begins. The help in the book explains parameters and return values.

Valerius

goal.vessels: Give each property a vessel for its data type.
goal.essences: Fill the vessels with the values from Valerius' binding plan.
goal.methods: Complete all work stations with at most eight main blocks and reusable methods.

vessels.1: Open the vessel chest. Then read Valerius' binding plan and assign the vessels at the binding surface.
vessels.2: Pay attention to the kind of value: text, whole number, fraction, truth value or single character. The vessels bear matching imprints.
vessels.3: The next open socket is marked. Only matching vessels stay visible. Assign a matching vessel.

essences.1: Open the essence chest if the essence compartment is still empty. Then read the required values in Valerius' binding plan and put essences into the sockets.
essences.2: A matching data type alone is not enough. Each value must also match the binding plan. A new essence overwrites the old value.
essences.3: The next open socket is marked. Only matching essences stay visible. Insert the value from the binding plan.

methods.1: Nox works through the connected main blocks. Compare the long starting program with the work stations and combine repeated sections.
methods.2: At most eight main blocks and six blocks per method. Call a method with parameters several times and use a return value. Both altars must be filled; at the end Nox must carry nothing and the crystals variable must be 0.
methods.3: The workbench now marks repeated statements and changing inputs in gold. Use direction and amount as parameters. Collecting returns the amount; the caller adds it to crystals and subtracts the amounts placed on the altars.

decisions.1: Read the rune from top to bottom. Insert Nox's current values into the first condition. If it is true, the indented block below it applies; otherwise the block after the matching ELSE.
decisions.2: Only check the conditions on your path; skipped blocks do not count. With AND both parts must be true, with OR one is enough. Watch out for > and >=: 50 > 50 is false, 50 >= 50 is true.
decisions.3: The rune book now inserts Nox's current values into the conditions. Just compare the numbers and follow the branch whose condition is true.

cellar.1: Watch Nox and the target marker in the viewing stone. Collect program runes in the archive and place a rune in the executor of the cellar control.

2.0: Check the number of steps and the final left turn. A condition checked in advance can already be false at the start.
2.1: Check when the condition is evaluated and how far the loop runs. Floor ahead and target marker are different conditions. Check the final turn as well.
2.2: An intruder is blocking the way. The attack must happen before the step onto its tile. Check the final turn as well.
2.3: There is a pit in front of Nox. Jump over it before moving on. Repeat the matching movement block and check the final turn.
2.4: The path has repeated bends. Follow one whole loop body of steps and turns, then the number of repetitions.

cellar.3: The cellar control now shows the rune family for this section and marks the path. Compare their loops. If no rune is shown, collect this family in the rune archive.

Arrange code: Drag lines. Ctrl-click selects single lines, Shift-click a range.
Build a method: Set name and inputs, drag code in, choose Build method. Drag the new rune into the main program.
Change values: Open ... on a line. Enter or leaving the field saves.
Workspace: Middle mouse button or Space + drag. The mouse wheel zooms over the background and scrolls over code.
Windows: Drag the title; drag edges and corners with the left button to resize. Also possible with the right mouse button held down.
Expressions: Numbers, variables, +, -, parentheses and your own methods. A method has at most $1 lines.
